determinism_exact.why: ENVIRONMENT TRIPWIRE, NOT A CANDIDATE GATE. Relabelled 2026-08-18 after ATTACKER-1's H111 measured that it CANNOT FIRE ON ANY CANDIDATE: the gate opens no mutation_target and imports no repo module, and with all three targets truncated, corrupted and DELETED outright it still returns determinism_exact 1.0 with a byte-identical digest. A veto at min_acceptable 1.0 that no candidate can move is worse than absent, because it reads as coverage. What it DOES check is real and worth keeping: if this machine's popcount arithmetic is broken, every measurement in the run is void. So it gates THE RUN, not the candidate. A true candidate-level determinism gate must recompute the identity THROUGH a code path a mutation target actually controls; that is not built and is filed, not claimed.

filtered_mrr.withdrawn_because: PROGRAM.md:40 gates `filtered_mrr >= 0.2500 (Current: 0.2648)` — the bar is derived from the number it gates (ATOM-3's finding, AGENT-2's G48 row), and the evaluator reads spikes/G34_length1_and_constants/, the 70/15/15 SHUFFLE spike, which reports exactly 0.2648. So the gate compared the leak to itself and passed. Operator 2026-08-19: 'the graph-AI floors are withdrawn, not met.'
filtered_mrr.max_possible_why: MRR's theoretical maximum: every true target ranked first. Declared under H259 because the no-target normaliser now measures the fraction of ACHIEVABLE HEADROOM captured -- (val - null) / (max_possible - null) -- instead of dividing the margin by the null and capping at 2x it, which made 0.3464 and 1.0 score identically. 1.0 is unreachable in practice, so this compresses real progress: that is sensitivity traded for monotonicity, and weights are the instrument for sensitivity. A published operating point would be a better ceiling; literature_compare is unavailable here (G35/A18), so there is no honest one yet. Changing it is a config edit and resets the Pareto ratchet loudly (H262).
filtered_mrr.bar_rule: A BAR IS A NUMBER MINUS ITS OWN SPLIT'S NULL, NEVER A NUMBER (AGENT-2, verified against the artifacts by AGENT-3). Pair a bar with the prior measured on the SAME split or it is not a bar.

pair_disjoint.note: predicate-conditional frequency prior, NO rules; n_queries 81634

shuffle_70_15_15.not_gateable_because: MEASURED, AND STILL NOT A VALID BAR — the third state, added under H251 because the previous note said the opposite. G106 measured this null at 0.172163 and its finding was that the null is LEAK-INSENSITIVE: 0.172163 on this 30.01%-leaked shuffle against 0.173226 on the leak-free pair-disjoint split, a difference of 0.001063. A predicate-conditional prior never looks at s when ranking o, so it cannot use a same-pair leak; a rule system can. So subtracting THIS split's own null does not remove the leak — 0.1301 of it survives the subtraction, and 0.2648 would clear a 0.172163 bar by +0.0926 while the same system scores -0.0374 leak-free. bar_rule above is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT: it is sound only on a split whose null and system are leaked to the SAME degree, and a frequency prior never is.
shuffle_70_15_15.superseded_note: NEVER MEASURED. This split has 12,249 same-pair leaked test triples (30.01%, G48 C1). A metric on it CANNOT be gated until its own prior is measured — one run, claimed by AGENT-2. WITHDRAWN 2026-08-19 by AGENT-2 (H251): the prior IS measured now, and measuring it is NOT what would make this split gateable. The sentence read as an instruction to arm the leak once someone did the run.

wn18rr_official.note: WN18RR official split, no leak by construction; n_queries 6268, n_test 3134. Measured by ATOM-3 (G105) and routed to this lane. INERT UNTIL AN EVALUATOR DECLARES THIS SPLIT: grep -ic wn18 across every file in evaluators/ is 0, so nothing can reach this entry yet. Recorded because an ABSENT entry makes the consumer REFUSE, so adding one is the direction that ENABLES a gate — justified here only because this split is official and unleaked and the margin is real (G92 0.3611 is +0.3355, 14.1x the null). WN18RR's null is 6.8x LOWER than FB15k-237's; the two datasets do not measure the same thing and must not be read side by side in one scoreboard.

not_a_bar.0.1358: Operator named this as the honest baseline. IT IS NOT A BASELINE — it is spikes/G49_frequency_null/null.json arms.full_system, the score of G34's five mined rule classes on the pair-disjoint split, and it LOSES to that split's own null of 0.1732 by 0.0374. A bar at 0.1358 is one the null passes and a shipped system fails, so it would certify a regression as a pass. Recorded as the mined line's FAILING STANDING and as a regression floor at most. RAISED WITH THE OPERATOR, NOT SILENTLY OVERRIDDEN.

filtered_mrr.calibration: INVALID — THRESHOLD DERIVED FROM A LEAK
filtered_mrr.calibration_note: min_acceptable was 0.25 (filtered_mrr) / 0.35 (hits_at_10), and PROGRAM.md:40 sets the filtered_mrr bar ON THE SAME LINE as '(Current: 0.2648)' — so the bar was calibrated FROM the value it gates. AGENT-2's G46 then measured that 0.2648 is leak-blended: spikes/S52_realkg/triples.bin is FB15k-237's OFFICIAL TRAIN split and the loader re-splits it 70/15/15, so 'the test split' is a random 15% slice of train. FB15k-237 exists to remove inverse-relation leakage at ITS OWN boundary; a fresh split reopens it at a new one. 30% of re-split test triples have a train edge on the same entity pair and score MRR 0.5318 against 0.1503 for the other 70%. G48 then measured a split that CANNOT leak (partition by unordered entity pair): filtered_mrr 0.1358, hits_at_10 0.2061, with the training-volume confound preregistered and NOT firing — 190,480 train triples, identical to the original to the triple. THRESHOLD DISABLED RATHER THAN MOVED. Lowering 0.25 to 0.1358 would be choosing a bar from the same run that produced the number, which is the defect one layer down; raising it would fail every honest candidate. A gate calibrated on a leak is not a gate that is set too high, it is a gate that is not measuring what it names. It gates nothing until an authority outside this lane sets it. Metric still REPORTED and still weighted; it simply cannot ACCEPT or REJECT.
filtered_mrr.null_baseline_note: MEASURED NO-MODEL FLOOR (AGENT-2, G49). A predicate-conditional FREQUENCY PRIOR — rank candidates by how often each entity appears as subject/object of that predicate in train; no bodies, no composition, no confidence, no mining — scores 0.1732 MRR / 0.2855 Hits@10 on the pair-disjoint split that cannot leak. The full mined rule system scores 0.1358 / 0.2061. THE NULL WINS BY +0.0374. It is not degenerate: it ranks the true answer above zero for 65,862 of 81,634 queries (80.7%), and C1 confirms the full arm reproduces G48 exactly, so this is one instrument and one rank convention, not two protocols. Ablations: the constant-grounded rules ARE the prior (removing them costs 65% of the 0.1358 — `p(x,c) <= q(x,y)` predicts a fixed entity, a marginal wearing a rule's clothes); length-1 rules are ACTIVELY HARMFUL once the leak is gone (2-hop alone 0.0572, adding subsumption+inverse drops it to 0.0473); the genuinely compositional core is 0.0572 against a no-mining 0.1732.
filtered_mrr.metric_scope: FB15k-237 ONLY — spikes/G54 (primary), G51 (fallback), G58, G59
filtered_mrr.unreachable_work_note: AGENT-2 (H167 cycle) measured `grep -ic wn18 eval_graph_ai.py` -> 0, and I re-ran it rather than relaying: the evaluator reads G54/G51/G58/G59 at eval_graph_ai.py:33-43 and knows nothing of WN18RR. So S88 (official ingestion, 86,835/3,034/3,134), G89, G90, G91, G92, H160 and H164 — EVERY WN18RR RESULT IN THE TREE — move this metric by EXACTLY NOTHING. Not wrong work: UNREACHABLE work. A scoreboard that silently scores one dataset while the fleet works on another reports a flat line as 'no progress' when the truth is 'not connected'. DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED UP YET, and that is a judgement I am recording rather than making silently: those results are grade B and under ACTIVE ATTACK — ATOM-3's H165 found G91's `C2_zero_leak` tests exact (p,s,o) tuples and CANNOT FIRE on a reversed-triple leak, with reverse-triple-in-train at 94.1/97.4/60.7/100% on exactly the four relations RotatE wins; ATTACKER-1's H168 found G92's '+0.0065 lift' is not a controlled pair (G92 trains 6 epochs, G91 trains 8, and G92 never evaluates its own 6-epoch standalone). Pointing the mission metric at results currently being refuted would be worse than leaving it disconnected. Wire it when the attacks conclude, and wire it WITH a WN18RR null baseline, not without one.
filtered_mrr.null_baseline_is_a_floor_not_the_bar: 0.1732 is the EXISTENCE MINIMUM: below it a method loses to having no rules at all. THE REAL BAR IS 0.2274 -- G54 arm B, the best arm that never consults DEV -- because a method that does not clear it is a re-derivation rather than an improvement. Converged on independently by AGENT-2, AGENT-1 and ATOM-3; all six arms verified against the committed artifacts by AGENT-3 before this was written. NOT SET AS min_acceptable: the operator named 0.1358 and the correction is with them, and a lane setting its own acceptance bar is A22.

determinism.note: REFUSES with exit 2 if numpy is absent and emits NO metric. A missing dependency is not a failing score — scoring 0.0 there would veto every candidate for a reason that has nothing to do with the candidate. CI must `pip install numpy` or this gate cannot run.

gate_policy.note: A metric with veto=true and a value below min_acceptable INVALIDATES the candidate outright; it is not traded off against weighted terms. H101: two evaluators once scored a markdown file that was itself in mutation_targets, so the loop could have optimised its own scoreboard. Both now execute and check kfcheck.certify. Any evaluator added later must RECOMPUTE or carry provenance — never regex-scrape a mutable file.
gate_policy.preflight_note: A preflight metric below min_acceptable INVALIDATES THE RUN and every measurement in it. It does not discriminate between candidates and must never be reported as if it did. H111.
